messages.subject: Model selection
parts:
Dear all
I am trying to fit a model to the detection function of my data. I have tried a 6 combinations of 2 models and 3 adjustment terms. I have 4 results of the six trials having the same value of AIC whic is also the least and with the same number of parameters used to fit the model.
So is there any way to judge the model selection if AIC & no. of parameters are equal to all.
Also CV is equal to all.
I hope if anybody can comment.

Husam El Alqamy.

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Model selection
parts:
Hi Hussam, list:

I would guess that some, if not all, of your 4 results that look the same are
in fact exactly the same model.

For example, say you set up 3 analyses with half-normal key function paired
with cosine, polynomial and hermite polynomial adjustments. Assume further
that you use the default method for choosing the adjustment terms in Distance,
which is sequential selection using AIC as the model selection criterion.
Let's imagine that in all 3 cases, the AIC for a model containing 1 adjustment
term is higher than the AIC where there are no adjustment terms. In that case,
Distance will choose a half-normal with no adjustment terms for all 3 analyses,
making the results exactly the same in all 3 cases.

The bottom line is that it's important to look through the Results tab of the
analysis details, particularly the Model Fitting page, to see exactly what
model was fit.

Hope this helps,

- Len Thomas
